# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT SEVEN GULLS POINT

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

The promised visit to Seven Gulls light was finally made by Nell and Hugh toward the end of September. Although they had frequently intended to make the trip, various obstacles continually arose to hinder them. At the small home, Captain Saul had “dropped in” on a few occasions.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0000 }

“Mistress Carrow, I am not one for formal manners,” he informed Nell. “Visiting this place brings me genuine joy, and I refuse to deprive myself simply on account of your not coming downstairs to meet me. Among those of us who understand each other, such conditions shouldn't exist. My visits will happen whenever possible, and yours will too, and provided that our agreeable small talk takes place, the particular shelter above us is of no consequence whatsoever.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0001 }

Captain Saul developed a strong fondness for Gog and Magog, who ruled over the hearth's fortunes in the small dwelling with the same degree of grace and composure as they had displayed at Tabby’s Place.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0002 }

“Aren’t they the cutest little cusses?” he used to inquire with delight; and with as much seriousness and regularity as he addressed his host and hostess, he offered them his greetings and goodbyes. Captain Saul had no intention of insulting domestic spirits through a deficit of veneration and formality.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0003 }

“This small home of yours is nearly flawless now,” he remarked to Nell. “In the past, it was never this lovely. Mistress Tremayne possessed a style like yours and accomplished marvelous things; yet people back then lacked the lovely small drapes, artwork, and ornaments that belong to you. Regarding Elizabeth, her existence was bound to former times. In a way, you’ve sort of introduced what lies ahead to this place. If conversation were entirely impossible for us when I visit, I’d still be truly joyful—simply remaining seated to gaze at you, along with your art and your blooms, would provide a sufficient pleasure. Beautiful—it’s just beautiful.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0004 }

Captain Saul possessed a fervent adoration for beauty. His existence was illuminated by a profound, delicate, interior delight derived from every beautiful sight or sound. Feeling a sharp consciousness regarding his personal absence of physical attractiveness, he mourned it.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0005 }

“People claim I have talent,” he mused playfully on a certain day, “yet I occasionally desire that the Lord had created me merely half as talented and allocated the remainder to my appearance. Even so, I suppose He understood His business, just as a capable Captain ought to. A few of us are required to be plain, or else the attractive individuals—such as Mistress Carrow right here—would not stand out so effectively.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0006 }

Eventually, Nell and Hugh strolled down to the Seven Gulls light during one evening. Gray cloud and mist had made for a gloomy start to the day, which nevertheless concluded with a magnificent display of gold and scarlet. Amber depths and clear, crystalline shallows lay above the western hills on the far side of the harbor, underpinned by the sunset’s blaze. Fiery little golden clouds formed a mackerel sky across the north. Gliding along the channel toward a southern port in a tropical palm country, a ship's white sails caught the glowing red light. Farther off, this illumination struck and turned blood-red the gleaming, white, vegetation-free surfaces of the sand dunes. Off to the right, it touched the ancient dwelling amidst the willows along the brook, briefly bestowing upon it windows more magnificent than those found in an old cathedral. Amid its serenity and drabness, they shone like the pulsating, crimson thoughts of a vibrant mind trapped inside a dreary shell of surroundings.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0007 }

“The ancient dwelling further up the stream continually appears so solitary,” Nell remarked. “I do not ever observe guests in that place. To be sure, its driveway leads out to the top thoroughfare—yet I do not believe there is a great deal of traffic. It appears strange that we have not hitherto encountered the Vanes, considering they reside less than a quarter-hour’s stroll from our home. Naturally, I might have caught sight of them at chapel, though had that occurred I failed to recognize them. I regret that they prove so distant, given that they represent our sole close neighbors.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0008 }

“It seems they aren't part of the group that recognizes Joseph,” Hugh chuckled. “Did you ever discover the identity of the young woman you considered so lovely?”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0009 }

“No. For some reason I have failed to inquire concerning her. Since I’ve never caught sight of her anywhere, though, I assume she was likely an unfamiliar face. Oh, the sun has only now disappeared—and the light has appeared.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0010 }

With the advancing twilight, broad beams were carved through the gloom by the massive lighthouse, rotating continuously across the meadows, the haven, the shoal, and the open sea.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0011 }

“It seems capable of seizing me and carrying me miles across the ocean,” Nell remarked, when a wave of brightness soaked them; and reaching a position so close to the Point that they were positioned within the radius of those blinding, repeating beams gave her a sense of relief.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0012 }

When they made the turn into the small lane leading to the Point through the fields, they encountered a man exiting it—a person whose look was so remarkable that both of them stared openly for a second. Tall, broad-shouldered, and with good features including a Roman nose and open gray eyes, he was unquestionably handsome; wearing a wealthy farmer’s finest Sunday clothes, he could, to this extent, have belonged to Seven Gulls or the Glen. However, a river of wavy brown beard cascaded down his chest almost reaching his knees, while a matching deluge of dense, rippling brown hair hung down his back from under his ordinary felt hat.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0013 }

“Nell,” whispered Hugh, as soon as they had moved beyond hearing distance, “did you happen to pour what Uncle Dave terms 'a little of the Scott Act’ into the lemonade you handed me right before we departed from the house?”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0014 }

“Indeed, I did not,” replied Nell, holding back her chuckles so the departing mystery wouldn't overhear. “Whatever person could he possibly be?”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0015 }

“I am uncertain; however, should Captain Saul maintain phantoms of that nature at this Point, carrying a piece of cold iron in my pocket will be my practice upon visiting. His lack of being a sailor prevents one from excusing his peculiar look; he ought to be a member of the over-harbor clans. According to Uncle Dave, a number of freaks reside in that place.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0016 }

“My opinion is that Uncle Dave holds a slight bias. As far as you are aware, every individual from over the harbor attending the Glen Church appears quite pleasant. Oh, Hugh, doesn’t this look lovely?”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0017 }

A projection of red sandstone precipice extending into the gulf served as the site for the Seven Gulls light. Extending across the channel on one flank lay the bar’s silvery sand shore; stretching along the opposite side was a lengthy, sweeping beach of red cliffs, which ascended sharply from the pebbled coves. Magic and mystery belonging to storm and star were familiar to this shore. A profound solitude exists around a coast like this. Solitude is never found in the woods—they overflow with whispering, beckoning, welcoming life. Conversely, the sea represents a mighty soul, perpetually lamenting a grand, unshareable grief, which confines it within its own existence for all eternity. Piercing its boundless mystery is impossible for us—we can merely roam, awed and spellbound, along its outermost border. A hundred voices call to us from the woods, whereas the sea possesses just one—a mighty voice that submerges our souls inside its majestic music. Human nature belongs to the woods, yet the sea resides among the ranks of the archangels.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0018 }

Nell and Hugh discovered Uncle Saul as he sat on a bench outdoors by the lighthouse, completing the final details of a magnificent, fully rigged toy schooner. Standing up, he greeted them at his dwelling with the soft, natural politeness that suited him so perfectly.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0019 }

“Every part of this day has been fairly lovely, Mistress Carrow, and currently, at its very end, the finest portion has arrived. Would you care to be seated out here for a short time, while daylight remains? Just now, I completed this small toy for Joe, my tiny grand nephew, up at the Glen. Subsequent to my agreement to construct it for him, I felt rather regretful, because his mother was annoyed. She fears he will desire to head out to sea in the future, and she prefers that the idea not be fostered within him. Nevertheless, what choice did I have, Mistress Carrow? I had PROMISED him, and to my mind, breaking a pledge made to a youngster is somewhat truly despicable. Come, take a seat. Spending an hour here will not require much time.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0020 }

Off the shore, the wind blew, doing no more than fracturing the ocean's face into lengthy, silvery ripples and causing gleaming shadows to hurry across it from each point and headland, resembling see-through wings. Over the headlands, where gulls gathered together, and the sand dunes, twilight suspended a veil of violet darkness. Scarves of silky mist thinly coated the sky. On the horizons, fleets of clouds floated at anchor. Above the bar, an evening star kept guard.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0021 }

“Is that not a sight that merits a look?” inquired Captain Saul, showing an affectionate, possessive pride. “It is comfortably distant from the market-place, is it not? No purchasing or vending or turning a profit. You are not charged a single cent—that entire expanse of ocean and firmament is costless—‘without money and without price.’ Furthermore, a moonrise will occur very shortly—discovering what a moonrise is capable of being above those rocks and water and harbor is something I never grow weary of. Each occasion contains an element of surprise.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0022 }

They observed the moon rise, taking in the wonder and enchantment of it silently, requiring nothing from one another or the world. After that, they climbed to the tower, where Captain Saul displayed and detailed how the large light's machinery operated. At last, they ended up in the dining room, in which a driftwood fire was creating flickering, subtle, ocean-tinted flames within the open hearth.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0023 }

“I built this hearth with my own hands,” Captain Saul observed. “Those in charge do not provide lighthouse keepers with these kinds of comforts. Notice the hues produced by that wood. Should you desire any driftwood for your hearth, Mistress Carrow, I will haul a supply up to you one of these days. Take a seat. I am preparing to brew a cup of tea for you.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0024 }

Captain Saul set down a seat for Nell, but only after he had cleared off a massive, orange-hued cat along with a newspaper.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0025 }

“Step down, Matey. Your spot is the sofa. I have to store this paper securely until I am able to locate the time for completing its tale. A Mad Love is its title. This kind of story is not my preferred type, yet I am only reading it to observe the extent to which she can prolong it. The sixty-second chapter has been reached, and from what I can tell, the marriage is not a bit closer than it was at the start. I must recite pirate tales to little Joe whenever he arrives. Isn't it odd that harmless young ones such as kids enjoy the most bloodthirsty tales?”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0026 }

“Just like Robin, my boy back home,” Nell remarked. “He desires stories dripping with blood.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0027 }

Captain Saul’s tea turned out to be nectar. Nell’s compliments made him as happy as a child, though he feigned a fine indifference.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0028 }

“My secret is that I am generous with the cream,” he nonchalantly observed. Captain Saul was unacquainted with Oliver Wendell Holmes, yet he clearly shared the perspective of that author's assertion that “big heart never liked little cream pot.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0029 }

“While drinking, Hugh remarked, “A strange-looking individual was walking out of your lane when we encountered him.” “Who could he be?””
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0030 }

A smirk appeared on Captain Saul's face.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0031 }

“Ambrose Kerr is that fellow—an exceptionally grand person who possesses merely a single strain of silliness. It crosses my mind that you were curious about his motive for making himself resemble a kind of cheap side-show oddity.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0032 }

“Does he represent a contemporary Nazarite, or is he an ancient Hebrew prophet remaining from long ago?” Nell inquired.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0033 }

“It is neither. Politics lies behind his oddity. Every one of those Kerrs, Crawfords, and MacAllisters is a politician through and through. Depending on the situation, their birth makes them Grit or Tory, their life is spent as Grit or Tory, and as Grit or Tory they pass away; and I cannot begin to understand what they will manage in heaven, where politics likely does not exist. Ambrose Kerr here entered the world as a Grit. As for me, I am a moderate Grit, yet moderation is something Ambrose lacks. A particularly fierce general election occurred fifteen years back. Tooth and nail, Ambrose campaigned for his side. He held absolute confidence in a Liberal victory—confidence so complete that he stood before a public gathering and swore he would avoid shaving his face or trimming his hair until power belonged to the Grits. Well, victory eluded them—and they have failed to achieve it to this day—and what you witnessed today was the consequence. Ambrose kept his promise.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0034 }

“How does his wife feel about it?” inquired Nell.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0035 }

“He isn't married. However, if a wife existed, I suppose she wouldn't be able to force him to violate that promise. The members of that Kerr family have constantly shown a resolve that exceeds what is natural. The brother of Ambrose, Alexander, possessed a dog that he valued immensely, and upon its death, the man truly desired for the animal to be interred within the cemetery, 'along with the other Christians,’ he stated. Naturally, permission was denied; consequently, he placed its grave right beyond the fence of the cemetery, and he refrained from ever crossing the church threshold again. Nevertheless, on Sundays he would transport his household to the church and remain seated near the grave of that dog, reading from his Bible throughout the duration of the service. People claim that as he was passing away, he requested that his spouse inter me near the dog; she possessed a timid, quiet nature, yet THAT made her spark with anger. She declared SHE refused to lie buried next to any dog, and if he preferred his final bed to be by the dog instead of by her, he only needed to state it. Alexander Kerr possessed the obstinacy of a mule, yet he cherished his spouse, so he yielded and stated, 'Well, durn it, bury me where you please. But when Gabriel’s trump blows I expect my dog to rise with the rest of us, for he had as much soul as any durned Kerr or Crawford or MacAllister that ever strutted.’ Those were HIS final spoken statements. Regarding Ambrose, everyone around here has grown accustomed to him, though he bound to appear extremely odd-looking to outsiders. My acquaintance with him began when he was ten years old—his age is roughly fifty currently—and I hold him in high regard. He and I were on the water cod-fishing today. That activity represents nearly everything I can manage these days—hooking the occasional trout and cod. Yet things were not always like this—definitely not in any way. I engaged in different pursuits in the past, a fact you would concede if you were to view my life-book.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0036 }

As Nell was on the verge of inquiring about the nature of his life-book, the First Mate caused a distraction by leaping onto Captain Saul’s knee. A magnificent creature, he possessed a face resembling a full moon in roundness, striking green eyes, and huge, double white paws. Captain Saul softly petted his velvety back.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0037 }

“Cats were never much to my liking until I came across the First Mate,” he observed, as the Mate purred exceedingly loud. “His life was saved by me, and a creature becomes impossible not to love once you have saved its life. Doing so is almost like bestowing life itself. The world contains some dreadfully unthinking individuals, Mistress Carrow. Certain city people owning summer residences across the harbor possess such a lack of thought that it amounts to cruelty. That unthinking variety is the most terrible form of cruelty. Coping with it is impossible. They maintain cats at those places throughout the summer, offering them food and affection, and decorating them with collars and ribbons. Then, upon the arrival of fall, they depart and abandon them to perish from hunger or cold. Mistress Carrow, my blood boils because of it. On a single day during this past winter, I discovered a miserable old mother cat lying dead upon the beach, her body pressed against her three tiny kittens who were nothing but skin and bone. Her death had occurred while attempting to protect them. Around them were wrapped her poor, rigid paws. I wept, Master. After that, I uttered curses. Following that, those poor little kittens were brought home by me, given plenty of food, and provided with good homes. The identity of the woman who abandoned the cat was known to me, and upon her return during the present summer, I simply crossed the harbor and expressed my view of her directly. My action was blatant interference, yet interfering for a worthy cause is something I truly enjoy.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0038 }

“In what manner did she react?” inquired Hugh.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0039 }

“She wept and mentioned that she ‘didn’t think.’ I told her, I says, ‘Is that going to be considered a proper justification on the day of Jedgment, when you are required to answer for the life of that poor old mother? I suppose the Lord will inquire why He bestowed brains upon you if they were not meant for thinking.’ I doubt she will abandon cats to die of hunger on another occasion.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0040 }

“Did the First Mate belong to the forsaken?” inquired Nell, offering him friendly overtures that he answered in a gracious, albeit patronizing, manner.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0041 }

“Yes. HIM I discovered on a freezing winter day, trapped in tree branches by his foolish ribbon collar. He had nearly starved. Mistress Carrow, if only you could have witnessed his eyes! Being merely a kitten, he had managed to survive on his own after being abandoned until he became entangled. Upon my freeing him, his tiny red tongue gave my hand a pathetic lick. The able seaman present today was not what he was then. As Moses, he was meek. Nine years have passed since that time. For a cat, his life in the land has been lengthy. The First Mate is a good old pal.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0042 }

“I ought to have anticipated that you would possess a dog,” Hugh remarked.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0043 }

A shake of his head came from Captain Saul.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0044 }

“A dog belonged to me once. My regard for him was so great that I was unable to endure the idea of replacing him with a new one after his death. A FRIEND was what he was—is that clear to you, Mistress Carrow? Matey is merely a pal. Matey has my affection—which is all the greater because of the hint of mischief inside him—as exists within every cat. My dog, however, possessed my LOVE. Alexander Kerr always had my secret compassion regarding HIS dog. A fine dog contains no devil at all. They are more worthy of love than cats for that reason, I suppose. Yet I'll be hanged if their interest equals a cat's. Look at me, speaking excessively. What stops you from stopping me? My speech flows terribly whenever an opportunity to converse with somebody comes my way. Provided your tea is finished, I possess some small items that may interest you to view—I acquired them in the strange places where I used to pry.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0045 }

The “few little things” belonging to Captain Saul proved to be a deeply fascinating assortment of curiosities—some grotesque, some peculiar, and some lovely. Furthermore, a remarkable tale was tied to nearly single one of them.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0046 }

The joy with which Nell heard those ancient stories on that moon-drenched night beside that spellbinding drift-wood flame was something she would always remember, as the silver ocean beckoned to them via the unclosed window and wept upon the stones beneath them.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0047 }

Captain Saul did not utter a single proud word, yet one could not avoid perceiving what an incredible hero the individual had proven to be—courageous, faithful, clever, selfless. Sitting there within his small room, he brought those events back to life for those who listened to him. Through an eyebrow's elevation, a lip's contortion, a motion, or a spoken word, he depicted an entire event or person in such a manner that they perceived it precisely as it occurred.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0048 }

A few of Captain Saul’s exploits possessed so extraordinary a quality that Hugh and Nell privately questioned whether he might be stretching the truth to take advantage of their trusting nature. However, as they subsequently discovered, they misjudged him in this regard. Every one of his stories was factually accurate. Captain Saul possessed the innate talent of a natural narrator, through which “unhappy, far-off things” are able to be conjured brightly for the listener in every bit of their original grief.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0049 }

His stories made Nell and Hugh laugh and tremble, and at one point tears came to Nell’s eyes. As Captain Saul observed her crying, delight radiated from his countenance.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0050 }

“I enjoy watching people weep in that manner,” he observed. “It pays a tribute. However, I am unable to do proper justice to the events I have witnessed or assisted in. I have written them all down in my life-book, yet I lack the skill to draft them correctly. Should I manage to find precisely the correct words and arrange them appropriately on paper, I could create a remarkable book. It would completely outdo A Mad Love, and I reckon Joe would enjoy it every bit as much as the pirate tales. Indeed, I have experienced several adventures during my life; and, tell me, Mistress Carrow, I continue to crave them. Indeed, despite how aged and worthless I am, a terrible yearning overcomes me occasionally to set sail out—out—out there—for all time.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0051 }

“Like Ulysses, you would
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0052 }

“Navigate past the sundown and the waters where every western star sets, right up to your death,’”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0053 }

Nell uttered in a dreamy manner.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0054 }

“Ulysses? His story is one I’ve read. Indeed, that accurately describes my emotions—exactly how every old seaman among us feels, I suppose. It seems I’m destined to pass away on dry land, I guess. Ah well, whatever happens is meant to happen. Consider old William Treleaven over at the Glen, who avoided going out on the water his entire existence due to his fear of drowning. A fortune-teller’s prophecy had foretold that fate for him. Then one day, losing consciousness, he collapsed face-first into the barn trough and drowned. Is it time for you to leave? Well, visit again quickly and visit frequently. The physician should be the one conversing on our next meeting. A great deal of information I wish to learn is known to him. I feel rather lonely in this place occasionally. The situation has deteriorated since Elizabeth Russell passed away. She and I were such close companions.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0055 }

Captain Saul expressed himself with the sorrowful emotion typical of the elderly, who observe their former companions gradually drifting away—companions who can never be truly replaced by individuals from a younger era, even those belonging to the group that recognizes Joseph. Nell and Hugh pledged that they would visit shortly and frequently.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0056 }

“Isn’t he a rare old fellow?” Hugh asked while they were walking home.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0057 }

“In some way, I am unable to align his gentle, easygoing nature with the reckless, daring existence he has led,” Nell reflected.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0058 }

“You would not consider it quite as difficult had you observed him recently in the lower fishing village. A member of Peter Gautier’s vessel uttered an unpleasant comment regarding a local young woman. Captain Saul almost incinerated the miserable man with the fierce glare of his eyes. He appeared to be a completely altered individual. His words were few—yet the manner in which he delivered them! It seemed powerful enough to peel the skin off the man's frame. I gather that Captain Saul does not permit any disparaging remark about any woman to be uttered near him.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0059 }

“I am curious why marriage never occurred for him,” Nell uttered. “He ought to possess sons whose vessels are currently out on the ocean, along with grandkids scrambling all over him to listen to his tales—that is the sort of person he is. Rather, he possesses merely a grand cat.”
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0060 }

However, Nell was wrong. Captain Saul possessed something beyond that. A memory was also his.
{: #nw-v04-c09-p0061 }
